title: The Man Who Crossed the Ocean Without a Compass
subtitle: Hawai'i to Tahiti, 1976
note: Fern stili sürekli anlatı: tek blok, her cümle tek fikir, cold open tarih + yer + somut eylem ile açar, son satır 12 kelimeden kısa cliffhanger. Vurgu *yıldız* ile işaretlenir; storyboard derleyicisi işaretsiz cümlelere kendi vurgusunu koyar.
narration: In 1976, a man named Mau Piailug stepped onto a double-hulled canoe in Hawai'i. He carried no compass, no charts, and no radio. He sailed from Hawai'i to Tahiti across four thousand kilometres of open water. Instead of instruments, he used the stars, the swell, and the flight of birds. Every night he read the sky. Every day he read the water. He had memorized two hundred and twenty star positions as a boy. Only five navigators of his tradition were still living. Thirty-three days later, the canoe reached Tahiti. Here is the strange part. In his mind, the canoe was never moving. He held it still, and let the islands come to him. Nobody had made that crossing for six hundred years.
